pathway.title: Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Assessment — Analyst Interpretation; confidence: Medium. TransDigm's engineered components, reported proprietary/aftermarket exposure, defense sales and positive historical operating cash support the business case. Documented debt-supported distributions and missing accessible-liquidity/legal evidence limit creditor confidence. The checked conditional FY2025 model has 3.14x reference earnings/cash-interest cover versus 2.28x downside, crossing a 3x analyst watch only in the downside; this is not covenant or actual forecast proof. Its assumed growth, margin, cash costs, repayment and excluded extra cash uses are conditions, not an issuer financing plan. Complete cash/access and refinancing sufficiency remain unassessed.

cells.text: Documentary Fact. TransDigm Group, through TransDigm Inc., designs, produces and supplies highly engineered aircraft components for commercial and military aviation; its businesses are managed in Power & Control, Airframe and Non-aviation segments.
S1 PDF 3–5. Segment descriptions and customer/channel scope are specified in Item 1.
Documentary Fact. The registrant is incorporated in Delaware, United States, and lists its principal executive office in Cleveland, Ohio; its operations and sales are global.
S1 PDF 1, 3–8. This identifies issuer country and principal office, not the location of every subsidiary.
Analyst Interpretation. Aerospace and defense components are the core sector, with smaller non-aviation activities.
S1 PDF 4–5 and 7. The label synthesizes disclosed product/end-market descriptions.
Management Language. Management says it focuses on pricing highly engineered products to reflect the value provided and resources required.
S1 PDF 4 and 6. This is the issuer's strategy description, not independent evidence of pricing power, realized pricing or cost pass-through.

Documentary Fact. Sales are made through OEM and aftermarket channels; business-unit teams combine product, engineering, operations, quality and sales functions. The issuer reports approximately 120 manufacturing facilities. Revenue is generally recognized at a point in time; limited customized contracts can qualify for over-time recognition.

S1 PDF 5–6, 120–122. This model requires manufacturing capacity, certified products and working capital; the filing does not disclose unit-level capacity utilization, order backlog, price/volume split or customer-level margins.

Insufficient Information where metrics are absent. Disclosed demand drivers include aircraft utilization, worldwide fleet age, RPKs, airline profitability and defense budget trends; raw material, labor and supply-chain costs are also identified as risks.

S1 PDF 3, 7, 10–11. No quantified volume, price realization, organic growth, backlog or input-cost pass-through dataset is supplied in the passages reviewed. Those measures remain null/not disclosed, not zero.

runs.text: Thesis — Analyst Interpretation. Continuing demand and cash conversion can support debt service, but financial policy and dated protection/funding changes determine how much reaches creditors. Better earnings alone do not establish liquidity after distributions. Conditional deleveraging depends on stipulated repayments and cash-use restraint; positive model cash, historical refinancing and reported hedge estimates do not prove current access or future execution.

Replacement-demand and channel breadth: actual CP-1A business analysis supports an issuer-estimated aftermarket/proprietary base and defense exposure alongside OEM sales. This can cushion new-build cyclicality; flight activity, customer economics and qualification/supply conditions still matter. Historical mix is not independently measured future pricing power.

Observed cash generation and execution: CP-1 and the actual CP-2D quarterly bridge show positive operating cash, while CP-1A documents historical financing. Those are real counterweights to a generic operating-collapse narrative; unrestricted access and future refinancing remain separate questions.

Dated rate mitigation: CP-2E preserves reported approximately 77% fixed-rate gross debt and an issuer approximately +30 USDm annual interest estimate for +100 bp at September 2024. Fixed coupons and derivatives mitigate selected repricing; the estimate was not independently rebuilt. Forward collars and expiring swaps/caps cannot be flattened into one permanent hedge ratio.

A concrete disconfirming cash case: CP-2G's stipulated 2-percentage-point higher-margin case raises first-year coverage to 3.26x versus reference 3.14x. This supports the positive mechanism if earnings convert and cash uses stay restrained; the higher margin is analyst judgment, not guidance or a probability.

Historical peer observations (literal increment): TDG reported group operating margin 44.47%, versus HEICO/CW 16.94–21.37%; N=2, median suppressed — Strengthens the historical reported-profitability observation. Business mix and accounting differences remain; no industry ranking or normalized margin premium is established. Moog segment profit does not fill its missing group subtotal. TDG CFO/sales 25.76%, versus selected peers 5.61–17.44%; N=3, median 17.43% — Adds a real reported-cash counterweight to an operating-weakness narrative. Customer funding and receivable-sale classification prevent treating the whole spread as underlying cash quality. TDG CFO minus gross cash PP&E capex 1,880 USDm, 23.68% of sales; peer ratios 1.28–15.92%, median 15.48%, N=3 — Supports observed cash generation after this specific investment line. It excludes acquisitions, finance-lease principal and other cash uses; it is not discretionary free cash or future debt repayment. The prior 1,880 proxy is unchanged.

Cash allocation competes with creditors: documented debt-supported distributions and the observed quarter's financing outflow reduce the buffer despite positive OCF. Declared, payable, single-event paid and quarterly amounts remain distinct. Current legal capacity and future policy are unknown.

Conditional debt-service pressure appears before the tested leverage watch: CP-2G's assumed 20% earnings reduction and 10% interest increase take FY2025 cover to 2.28x versus reference 3.14x, below the 3x analyst watch. The model also stipulates growth 11.46% then 5%/5%, margin 52.94%, cash-interest rate 6%, tax/WC share 10%, capex share 2%, annual repayments 1,000, the approximate October distribution 4,348 and no extra distributions/M&A/buybacks/borrowing. Those cash assumptions and exclusions are not sourced issuer plans; the result is neither a covenant breach nor a calibrated forecast.

Positive model cash does not prove liquidity: CP-2G's FY2025 closing cash is 3,043.36 reference and 1,957.05 downside, but accessible liquidity and minimum cash remain null. Annual endpoints omit troughs, complete maturities/securitization/leases, financing and noncash debt movements. The 7x analyst leverage watch is not reached by FY2027 under assumed repayments; this does not prove obligations are funded.

Earnings and debt definitions constrain comparisons: recurring/heterogeneous adjustments leave quality earnings unresolved. Carrying debt, gross principal and the known lease/pension subtotal differ. Neither issuer EBITDA nor an engine cash proxy is sustainable FCF, covenant or agency capacity; source interest/tax provisions are not cash payments.

Operating and environmental cash risks need targeted monitoring: CP-2E/CP-2F identifies cost recovery, supply/safety, physical/transition and actual environmental liability 41 (prior 44). Estimate/payment changes could consume cash, but the liability is not an incremental loss. Preserve the issuer's contrary expectation about excess costs; no new realised safety event, ESG score, greenium or debt ratchet is established.

Peer comparison restrictions (literal increment): TDG carrying borrowing/finance-lease bridge 24,880 USDm / annual CFO = 12.17x; peers 1.94–4.86x, median 3.32x, N=3 — Keeps the large reported borrowing base visible beside high cash margins. This is not Debt/EBITDA, covenant leverage, years to repay or a normalized rating ratio. Financing/CFO classification differences prohibit an economic-debt credit ranking. Capex/sales TDG 2.08%, peer range 1.51–4.32%; Moog 4.32% — TDG is inside this selected range. Moog's investment/contract cash pattern is a real difference, not a bad datapoint removed to tighten the range. No maintenance-capex advantage is inferred. Three Web-Scraped — Unverified selection judgments; primary financial facts separately checked — Confidence in the literal statements/arithmetic is stronger than confidence that these three form the correct complete peer group. No user-approved/industry-wide conclusion follows.

blocks.title: Company profile

cells.text: Publicly traded issuer with common shares; the reviewed annual report does not establish a controlling shareholder or provide enough evidence here to assign an owner percentage or sponsor. Management and Board have issuer-level roles, but individual directors are not scored.

Insufficient Information for beneficial ownership concentration, voting agreements, sponsor ownership or controlling-person economics. S1 PDF 61 defers beneficial-ownership information to the incorporated Proxy Statement; CP-1 T4.4/T4.6 share counts and stockholders’ deficit do not establish ownership percentages. Do not infer private-equity ownership. Obtain and review the incorporated Proxy Statement beneficial-ownership table, then any voting/ownership agreements needed to resolve control.
Not established in the reviewed filing passages. The filing states the company began in 1993 and reports a public-company structure, but this is not a full ownership-change history.
Insufficient Information. No ownership-change timeline or sponsor-control documentation is inferred from acquisitions, financing or issuer reputation.

Documentary Fact. The filing reports management's estimate that approximately 90% of FY2024 net sales were generated by proprietary products. This is a reported estimate, not an independently verified calculation.
S1 PDF 4. Proprietary product design can support differentiation; the filing does not quantify price elasticity, competitive wins or price-cost recovery.

Documentary Fact. The filing reports that approximately 55% of FY2024 net sales came from aftermarket. It estimates a typical platform production period of 20 to 30 years, aircraft life of approximately 25 to 30 years and product life cycle in excess of 50 years. These are issuer estimates.

S1 PDF 4. Installed-base consumption over aircraft life can support replacement demand; the estimate does not establish future demand. Contrary evidence: commercial aftermarket demand depends on flight hours, RPKs, fleet age and airline profitability; defense demand depends on budgets and political factors (PDF 7).
Management Language. Management characterizes aftermarket revenues as historically higher gross profit and more stable than OEM net sales.
S1 PDF 4. This historical characterization is not an independent forecast or measured future margin guarantee; demand-cycle exposures in PDF 7 remain.

Documentary Fact. FY2024 sales were approximately 31% commercial/regional/business/general aviation aftermarket, 27% commercial aerospace OEM, 40% defense, and 2% non-aerospace. Top ten customers were approximately 42% of sales; no single customer exceeded 10%.

S1 PDF 7. Customer diversification by individual counterparty coexists with end-market concentration and cyclicality. The filing does not supply contract backlog or customer-specific revenue trends here.

The filing does not allocate exact borrowed dollars to the transaction or supply pro forma leverage. Measurement-period estimates remained subject to adjustment (PDF 116).; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: May 21, 2024 — Completed; Transaction and parties: SEI Industries stock acquisition; included in Airframe.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: Approximately $171 million cash, including $1 million working-capital settlement; financed from existing cash on hand (S1 PDF 117).; Credit relevance and limitation: Cash deployment and integration; measurement period remained open; no deal-level post-acquisition results or return analysis supplied.; Category: Documentary Fact

No pro forma sales/results supplied because stated not material (PDF 118).; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: FY2024 — Completed; Transaction and parties: Extant Aerospace product-line acquisitions of substantially all assets and technical data rights, included in Power & Control.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: Total purchase price $86 million (S1 PDF 119–120); funding source not separately stated in the passage reviewed.; Credit relevance and limitation: Disclosed repeated product-line acquisitions, but one year does not establish future appetite. Allocation remained preliminary.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: May 8, 2023 — Completed; Transaction and parties: Calspan Corporation stock acquisition; included in Airframe.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: Approximately $730 million cash including $1 million FY2024 working-capital settlement; financed from existing cash (S1 PDF 118).; Credit relevance and limitation: Purchase accounting was adjusted during the measurement period; the filing describes a transonic wind tunnel valuation change. No pro forma sales/results supplied because stated not material (PDF 118–119).; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: FY2023 — Completed; Transaction and parties: Extant Aerospace product-line acquisitions.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: Total purchase price $24 million (S1 PDF 120); funding source not separately stated in the passage reviewed.; Credit relevance and limitation: Further documented acquisition activity; does not alone prove appetite or successful integration.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: November 28, 2023 — Completed financing; Transaction and parties: Amendment No. 13 issued $1,000 million Tranche J loans, fully drawn; $1,000 million 2031 secured notes were also issued.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: S1 PDF 127–128 says proceeds plus cash were used primarily to fund CPI. CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 net term-loan proceeds 6,815 and net senior secured note proceeds 7,373 USD millions for all FY2024 activity; these are not deal-level principal amounts.; Credit relevance and limitation: Funding and maturity profile changed; no current headroom or pro forma leverage calculation is made.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: February 27, 2024 — Completed Amendment 14; Transaction and parties: Revolving facility refinanced: maturity extended to February 2029, commitments increased and applicable margin decreased (S1 PDF 128).; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: CP-1 T4.5 annual net cash proceeds and repayment rows do not isolate the amendment.; Credit relevance and limitation: Changes available facility term/cost; does not establish current availability beyond reported figures.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: March 22, 2024 — Completed Amendment 15 / new notes; Transaction and parties: Tranche I term loans repriced; Tranche H repaid and replaced by Tranche K. Additional $550 million 2029 secured notes issued (S1 PDF 129–130).; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 net note/term-loan proceeds and repayments as annual inflows/outflows, not gross principal or deal-level funding.; Credit relevance and limitation: Changes pricing/maturity and funding profile; no pro forma leverage or full creditor-class impact is inferred.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: March 28, 2024 — Completed note redemption; Transaction and parties: $4,400 million 2026 secured notes redeemed using net proceeds of 2029/2032 note offerings plus cash (S1 PDF 129).; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 net senior-secured-note proceeds 7,373 and repayments (4,400) USD millions; these are annual cash-flow lines.; Credit relevance and limitation: Refinanced maturity; amounts are not net debt change or proof of future refinancing capacity.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: April 22, 2024 — Completed note redemption; Transaction and parties: $550 million 2027 senior subordinated notes redeemed using net proceeds from the additional 2029 secured notes plus cash (S1 PDF 130).; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: CP-1 T4.5 aggregates annual proceeds/repayments.; Credit relevance and limitation: Changes debt structure; no class-by-class outcome is inferred.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: June 4, 2024 — Completed Amendment 16; Transaction and parties: Tranche J repriced; $2,644 million of Tranche I term loans amended and extended into Tranche J maturing February 2031 (S1 PDF 130).; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 net term-loan proceeds 6,815 and repayments (4,403) USD millions, not principal amounts for this amendment.; Credit relevance and limitation: Maturity and pricing changed; no creditor-treatment conclusion absent operative terms and effect analysis.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: September 19, 2024 — Completed financing / dividend funding; Transaction and parties: Issued $1,500 million 2033 secured notes and $1,500 million Tranche L loans, fully drawn; issuer states proceeds from both fourth-quarter issuances plus existing cash funded the $75.00-per-share special dividend declaration.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: S1 PDF 131; CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 net senior-secured-note proceeds 7,373 and net term-loan proceeds 6,815 USD millions across the year. CP-1 T4.18 maturity schedule is historical principal excluding finance leases, not a current refinancing forecast.; Credit relevance and limitation: This directly documents debt proceeds supporting a shareholder distribution; exact tracing, legal capacity and post-distribution liquidity remain unassessed.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: July 12, 2024 — Completed amendment; Transaction and parties: Securitization facility capacity increased from $450 million to $650 million and maturity extended to July 11, 2025; issuer reported $487 million drawn at September 30, 2024.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: S1 PDF 130; CP-1 T4.6 separately reports securitization carrying value of 486 USD millions at September 30, 2024. Principal and carrying value differ.; Credit relevance and limitation: Receivables-backed borrowing capacity is financing, not cash on hand; October draw is a subsequent event.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: FY2024 — Completed, distribution; Transaction and parties: Special cash dividends declared at $35.00 per share in November 2023 and $75.00 per share on September 19, 2024.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: S1 reports $6,153 million total declared special dividends, with $1,937 million paid during FY2024 and $4,216 million accrued at year-end; the $4,216 million dividend and $132 million equivalents were paid in October 2024 (S1 PDF 146). Proceeds from both fourth-quarter debt issuances plus existing cash funded the September declaration (PDF 131); a separate disclosure says $3,000 million new senior secured debt and cash funded the approximately $4,348 million October payment (PDF 29). The November $35.00 payment was funded by existing cash (PDF 29). CP-1 T4.5 reports FY2024 dividend/equivalent cash payments (2,038) USD millions; T4.6 reports dividends payable 4,216 at September 30, 2024.; Credit relevance and limitation: Debt funding is documented for the September declaration, not November. Exact proceeds tracing, contractual capacity and post-payment liquidity remain unassessed. Declarations, fiscal-year payments and payable are distinct measures.; Category: Documentary Fact

Period / status: FY2022 — Completed, distribution / repurchase; Transaction and parties: Statement of changes in stockholders’ deficit reports special dividends and vested equivalents declared (1,045) USD millions and stock repurchases (912) USD millions; CP-1 cash flow reports dividends and equivalents paid (1,091) and repurchases (912) USD millions.; Consideration / funding stated by issuer: S1 PDF 108–109; CP-1 T4.4 and T4.5.; Credit relevance and limitation: Documents earlier cash/equity extraction, but the declaration/payment distinction and FY2022 source-of-funds limitation remains.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: 1993; Issuer-level event: Company states it was founded; it reports 93 acquired businesses/product lines since then.; Status and credit significance: Historical statement in S1 PDF 4; not a transaction-by-transaction ownership history.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: FY2022; Issuer-level event: Special dividend/equivalent declarations and stock repurchase are reported in equity and cash-flow statements.; Status and credit significance: Completed. Evidence of shareholder extraction; funding source and legal capacity are not established for these FY2022 actions.; Category: Documentary Fact
Date / period: May 8, 2023; Issuer-level event: Calspan acquisition completed.; Status and credit significance: Completed; see transaction summary.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: FY2024, dates specified by deal in Note 2; Issuer-level event: FPT, SEI, CPI Electron Device Business, Raptor Scientific and Extant product-line acquisitions completed; Extant product-line note states FY2024 only.; Status and credit significance: Completed; see transaction summary. Do not assign Extant acquisitions the dates of other deals.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: November 2023 / September 19, 2024; Issuer-level event: $35.00 and $75.00 special dividends per share declared; November payment from existing cash; September declaration funded by proceeds from both fourth-quarter issuances plus existing cash.; Status and credit significance: Completed declarations; October payment is subsequent to year-end. S1 PDF 29, 131, 146.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: October 2024; Issuer-level event: The $4,216 million dividend and $132 million equivalents were paid. CP-1 also identifies an October draw of remaining $162.5 million securitization availability.; Status and credit significance: The debt was raised in September and funded the September declaration; cash payment was post-period. S1 PDF 29, 131 and 146.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: February 27, March 22, March 28, April 22 and June 4, 2024; Issuer-level event: Amendments 14–16, note issues and redemptions, at the dates stated in the transaction table.; Status and credit significance: Completed financing actions in S1 PDF 128–130; no creditor-class effects are assessed here.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: July 12, 2024; Issuer-level event: Securitization facility amendment increased capacity and extended maturity.; Status and credit significance: Completed; S1 PDF 130.; Category: Documentary Fact

Date / period: September 19, 2024; Issuer-level event: Issued $1,500 million 2033 secured notes and $1,500 million Tranche L loans; both issuances plus existing cash funded the $75.00 declaration.; Status and credit significance: Debt raised and dividend declared in September; cash distribution occurred in October. S1 PDF 29 and 131.; Category: Documentary Fact

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Assessment — Analyst Interpretation; confidence: Medium.** TransDigm's engineered components, reported proprietary/aftermarket exposure, defense sales and positive historical operating cash support the business case. Documented debt-supported distributions and missing accessible-liquidity/legal evidence limit creditor confidence. The checked conditional FY2025 model has 3.14x reference earnings/cash-interest cover versus 2.28x downside, crossing a 3x analyst watch only in the downside; this is not covenant or actual forecast proof. Its assumed growth, margin, cash costs, repayment and excluded extra cash uses are conditions, not an issuer financing plan. Complete cash/access and refinancing sufficiency remain unassessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Thesis — Analyst Interpretation.** Continuing demand and cash conversion can support debt service, but financial policy and dated protection/funding changes determine how much reaches creditors. Better earnings alone do not establish liquidity after distributions. Conditional deleveraging depends on stipulated repayments and cash-use restraint; positive model cash, historical refinancing and reported hedge estimates do not prove current access or future execution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. **Replacement-demand and channel breadth:** actual CP-1A business analysis supports an issuer-estimated aftermarket/proprietary base and defense exposure alongside OEM sales. This can cushion new-build cyclicality; flight activity, customer economics and qualification/supply conditions still matter. Historical mix is not independently measured future pricing power.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. **Observed cash generation and execution:** CP-1 and the actual CP-2D quarterly bridge show positive operating cash, while CP-1A documents historical financing. Those are real counterweights to a generic operating-collapse narrative; unrestricted access and future refinancing remain separate questions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. **Dated rate mitigation:** CP-2E preserves reported approximately 77% fixed-rate gross debt and an issuer approximately +30 USDm annual interest estimate for +100 bp at September 2024. Fixed coupons and derivatives mitigate selected repricing; the estimate was not independently rebuilt. Forward collars and expiring swaps/caps cannot be flattened into one permanent hedge ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. **A concrete disconfirming cash case:** CP-2G's stipulated 2-percentage-point higher-margin case raises first-year coverage to 3.26x versus reference 3.14x. This supports the positive mechanism if earnings convert and cash uses stay restrained; the higher margin is analyst judgment, not guidance or a probability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. **Historical peer observations (literal increment):** TDG reported group operating margin 44.47%, versus HEICO/CW 16.94–21.37%; N=2, median suppressed — Strengthens the historical reported-profitability observation. Business mix and accounting differences remain; no industry ranking or normalized margin premium is established. Moog segment profit does not fill its missing group subtotal. TDG CFO/sales 25.76%, versus selected peers 5.61–17.44%; N=3, median 17.43% — Adds a real reported-cash counterweight to an operating-weakness narrative. Customer funding and receivable-sale classification prevent treating the whole spread as underlying cash quality. TDG CFO minus gross cash PP&E capex 1,880 USDm, 23.68% of sales; peer ratios 1.28–15.92%, median 15.48%, N=3 — Supports observed cash generation after this specific investment line. It excludes acquisitions, finance-lease principal and other cash uses; it is not discretionary free cash or future debt repayment. The prior 1,880 proxy is unchanged.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. **Cash allocation competes with creditors:** documented debt-supported distributions and the observed quarter's financing outflow reduce the buffer despite positive OCF. Declared, payable, single-event paid and quarterly amounts remain distinct. Current legal capacity and future policy are unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. **Conditional debt-service pressure appears before the tested leverage watch:** CP-2G's assumed 20% earnings reduction and 10% interest increase take FY2025 cover to 2.28x versus reference 3.14x, below the 3x analyst watch. The model also stipulates growth 11.46% then 5%/5%, margin 52.94%, cash-interest rate 6%, tax/WC share 10%, capex share 2%, annual repayments 1,000, the approximate October distribution 4,348 and no extra distributions/M&A/buybacks/borrowing. Those cash assumptions and exclusions are not sourced issuer plans; the result is neither a covenant breach nor a calibrated forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. **Positive model cash does not prove liquidity:** CP-2G's FY2025 closing cash is 3,043.36 reference and 1,957.05 downside, but accessible liquidity and minimum cash remain null. Annual endpoints omit troughs, complete maturities/securitization/leases, financing and noncash debt movements. The 7x analyst leverage watch is not reached by FY2027 under assumed repayments; this does not prove obligations are funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. **Earnings and debt definitions constrain comparisons:** recurring/heterogeneous adjustments leave quality earnings unresolved. Carrying debt, gross principal and the known lease/pension subtotal differ. Neither issuer EBITDA nor an engine cash proxy is sustainable FCF, covenant or agency capacity; source interest/tax provisions are not cash payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. **Operating and environmental cash risks need targeted monitoring:** CP-2E/CP-2F identifies cost recovery, supply/safety, physical/transition and actual environmental liability 41 (prior 44). Estimate/payment changes could consume cash, but the liability is not an incremental loss. Preserve the issuer's contrary expectation about excess costs; no new realised safety event, ESG score, greenium or debt ratchet is established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. **Peer comparison restrictions (literal increment):** TDG carrying borrowing/finance-lease bridge 24,880 USDm / annual CFO = 12.17x; peers 1.94–4.86x, median 3.32x, N=3 — Keeps the large reported borrowing base visible beside high cash margins. This is not Debt/EBITDA, covenant leverage, years to repay or a normalized rating ratio. Financing/CFO classification differences prohibit an economic-debt credit ranking. Capex/sales TDG 2.08%, peer range 1.51–4.32%; Moog 4.32% — TDG is inside this selected range. Moog's investment/contract cash pattern is a real difference, not a bad datapoint removed to tighten the range. No maintenance-capex advantage is inferred. Three Web-Scraped — Unverified selection judgments; primary financial facts separately checked — Confidence in the literal statements/arithmetic is stronger than confidence that these three form the correct complete peer group. No user-approved/industry-wide conclusion follows.
